name: Colombia
sources: GDP $47.8bn and 32.4m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $47.844bn and 32,440,069). Colombia is the one Latin American economy that never defaulted and never had a lost decade: it grew every year of the 1980s, hence a positive TFP trend of 0.8%/yr.

Inflation 29.1% is the DANE CPI annual average for 1990 (December-on-December 32.4%, the highest print since 1963), driven by the crawling-peg devaluation. interest_rate 36% is the DTF deposit benchmark; Banco de la Republica gains its independence in the 1991 constitution, which is not scripted here.
Tax take 14% of GDP, low even for the region and the reason the Gaviria government's 1990 reform mattered. Gross fixed capital formation about 19% of GDP.
Debt 0.42: external debt $17.2bn at end-1990 (World Bank), about 36% of GDP, serviced in full throughout — Colombia stayed out of the Baker and Brady processes on purpose.
Oil 0.44 mbd: about 445,000 bbl/d in 1990, Cano Limon and Cusiana coming on, Ecopetrol majority. The Cano Limon pipeline was bombed by the ELN roughly forty times that year.

Defence 2.1% of GDP and strength 7: an army with no external mission and three internal wars. Stability 32 is the lowest in this region and it is transcription, not colour — the Medellin cartel had killed presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galan in August 1989, bombed Avianca Flight 203 in November, and killed two more candidates, Bernardo Jaramillo and Carlos Pizarro, in March and April 1990.
Separatism 0.10: FARC, ELN and EPL held territory rather than claiming secession, so the strain is real but not a national question on the Yugoslav scale.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.0981%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series COL (Colombia): 28,642,690 in 1984 to 31,776,279 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 3.862 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, COL, 1989: US$3862357243.88 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: COL.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 88% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: COL, 1990 = 88%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name. The 1989 value of the same series is 78%, on the other side of the 80% line: THRESHOLD-SENSITIVE CELL.
